messages:
maya: Hi team — enterprise customer `acme-inc` reports tool calls failing after a recent rename. They call `TranslateText` (capital T) via our API and get 404/ToolNotFound. Repro steps from them: 1) POST /v1/toolcall with {
  "tool_name": "TranslateText",
  "args": { "text": "hola", "to": "en" }
}
Response: 404 { "error": "tool not found", "code": "tool_lookup_failed" }. Ticket #T-9813. Anyone seen rename propagation issues? :thinking_face:

kevin (customer): Confirmed this worked before rename last week. We tried the alias `translate_text` and that worked — but our SDK auto-uses the old PascalCase name. We need a fix or a suggestion for a safe fallback.

olivia: Thanks @maya — checking logs for their org id. Can you paste the request id or x-request-id from client?

maya: Request id from the failing run: `req_0a7c3f2b`. Also they included `x-org-id: acme-inc` and `x-client-sdk: ruby-1.4.2`. Full failing response header snippet: `x-rw-trace: rwt-4f2c; x-registry-version: v2026-03-12-18`

sanjay: grabbing registry watcher logs for that window. Initial hypothesis: name normalization/casing mapping didn't propagate to the tool-name -> uuid index on the public lookup nodes. We had a rolling rename job last week that wrote canonical `translate_text` and new alias `TranslateText`. Some caches are case-sensitive.

ops-bot: detected registry write: rename op id `op_2209` applied 2026-03-11T22:11:08Z to modeltools catalog. 12 of 48 lookup nodes reported ACK; 36 reported delayed ack.

olivia: If it's cache TTL, a quick workaround is to call by tool UUID or use lowercase alias. Can the SDK fall back to case-insensitive lookup? For now tell them to set `tool_id` param.

kevin (customer): We can patch client but need a server-side solution for other users. Their traffic spikes and we can't force all clients to change immediately.

maya: I gave them `tool_id: tool_876a9` which worked. But we need root cause so it doesn't keep happening.

sanjay: Found watcher logs: the rename event was processed but the alias-sync job failed with `Err: duplicate key on write` on cluster nodes that were under heavy load. Those nodes then rolled back to previous index state and their in-memory mapper remained missing the PascalCase alias. The fallback logic only matches exact keys if present. I'll push a patch to make lookup case-folding on the mapper layer and add a mitigation to accept alias in lower/upper.

olivia: Patch sounds good. Can we also add a temporary api gateway middleware that does case-insensitive alias resolution for lookups older than registry version `v2026-03-12-00`?

sanjay: Yes. Plan: 1) Hotfix middleware to perform case-insensitive check + histogram to measure hits (evict after 24h). 2) Run a backfill reconcile job to reindex aliases on the 36 lagging nodes (script below). 3) Add stricter write-time idemp check to prevent duplicate-key rollback.

# Reindex script (ops):
```
for node in $(cat lagging_nodes.txt); do
  ssh $node 'service tool-mapper stop; ./reindex-tool-aliases --org acme-inc --force; service tool-mapper start'
 done
```

ops-bot: enqueued job `reindex_job_374` to run on next maintenance window (in 10m).

kevin (customer): Appreciate the quick mitigation. Please keep us posted on SLA impact. Current failing calls were ~8% of their traffic.

maya: I told them: use `tool_id` as temporary workaround, expect a hotfix in ~30m, reindex job will clear stale nodes in next maintenance window.

olivia: I'll own the postmortem and add a note to the SDK docs recommending clients pass `tool_id` where possible. Also will add an alert for registry write ack percent < 95% so we detect partial rollouts earlier.

sanjay: Deployed middleware hotfix to prod canary. Early metric: 95% of previously failing requests now map correctly (case-insensitive matcher). Reindex job starting in 2m.

maya: Thanks all — I'll update the customer and close the ticket once reindex finishes and we see 0 errors for 30m. :white_check_mark:
